'COULD NOT CHECK' vs 'CHECKED AND FOUND NOTHING' - hunted, nothing introduced. Both git calls the new code depends on (lwb_lanes.commit_files and the rewritten _authors) use subprocess check=True, so a git failure raises and exits loudly instead of returning an empty list that would read as a clean pass. _is_record_only_commit also returns False on an empty file list, so the failure direction is strict, not permissive.

NON-BLOCKING OBSERVATION, PRE-EXISTING, EXPLICITLY NOT CHARGED TO THIS PR. commit_files() runs `git diff-tree --no-commit-id --name-only -r --root <sha>`, which emits NOTHING for a merge commit. I confirmed commit_files('752269c...') == [] and confirmed the function is byte-identical in origin/main, so #45 does not introduce this. In check_lanes a merge commit therefore reads as touching zero files, touches_shared stays False, and no independent review is demanded of the merge commit itself. On #45 this is harmless: _is_record_only_commit correctly returns False on the empty list, so the merge IS the reviewable head and every record must name it (which is why this record exists), and the nine content commits demand review on their own. The residual hole is a hypothetical PR whose ONLY shared-path change arrives inside a merge commit's conflict resolution - touches_shared would never be True for any commit and the review gate would never fire at all. That deserves its own item; it is not a reason to block this PR.
